title: Romans Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 11.

questions.question: What tribe does Paul claim to be from in Romans 11?
questions.explanation: Paul identifies himself as of the tribe of Benjamin in Romans 11:1.

questions.question: According to Romans 11:2, has God cast away his people?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:2 states that God has not cast away his people which he foreknew.

questions.question: How many men has God reserved who have not bowed to Baal according to Romans 11:4?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:4 tells us that God has reserved seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 11:5 states there is a remnant according to the election of grace.
questions.explanation: Romans 11:5 confirms that there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:6 say about grace?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:6 explains that if it is by grace, then it is no more of works.

questions.question: True or False: According to Romans 11:7, Israel has obtained what it seeks.
questions.explanation: Romans 11:7 states that Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for.

questions.question: In Romans 11:10, what is said about their eyes?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:10 states, 'Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see.'

questions.question: What effect did Israel's fall have according to Romans 11:11?
options: It led to salvation for the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It led to salvation for the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Romans 11:11 indicates that through Israel's fall, salvation has come unto the Gentiles.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 11:12 states that the fall of Israel is the riches of the world.
questions.explanation: Romans 11:12 explains that the fall of Israel be the riches of the world.

questions.question: What does Paul magnify in Romans 11:13?
questions.explanation: In Romans 11:13, Paul states that he magnifies his office as the apostle of the Gentiles.

questions.question: In Romans 11, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: God has not cast away his people
questions.correctAnswer: God has not cast away his people
questions.explanation: Romans 11:2 discusses that God has not cast away his people, which is one of the first points made in the chapter.

medium.title: Romans Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:13 indicate about Paul's role in relation to the Gentiles?
options: He is the apostle of the Gentiles
He is a prophet to Israel
He is a teacher of the law
He is a missionary to the Samaritans
questions.correctAnswer: He is the apostle of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Paul states, 'For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles' (Romans 11:13), affirming his role as a messenger to the Gentiles.

questions.question: According to Romans 11:15, what is the result of the casting away of the people?
options: It leads to reconciliation of the world
questions.correctAnswer: It leads to reconciliation of the world
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world,' indicating that their rejection leads to salvation for others.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:20 warn about the wild olive branches?
options: They are better than the natural branches
They should fear because of unbelief
They will be cut off from the olive tree
They are to boast over the natural branches
questions.correctAnswer: They should fear because of unbelief
questions.explanation: The text states, 'Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear' (Romans 11:20), emphasizing humility and caution.

questions.question: How does Romans 11:22 describe God's nature toward those who have fallen?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness' (Romans 11:22), highlighting God's dual nature.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:23 say about the natural branches if they do not persist in unbelief?
options: They shall be graffed in again
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be graffed in again
questions.explanation: The verse affirms, 'And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again' (Romans 11:23), indicating hope for restoration.

questions.question: According to Romans 11:24, how does the natural olive tree compare to the wild olive tree?
options: The wild olive tree is superior
The natural olive tree is better for grafting
The wild olive tree cannot be grafted
The natural olive tree is contrary to nature
questions.correctAnswer: The natural olive tree is better for grafting
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that those who are natural branches should be graffed into their own olive tree, suggesting their inherent value in God's plan (Romans 11:24).

questions.question: What does Romans 11:28 indicate about the relationship between the gospel and Israel?
options: They are enemies for the Gentiles' sake
They are friends of the Gentiles
They have no bearing on the Gentiles
They are indifferent to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: They are enemies for the Gentiles' sake
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers' sakes' (Romans 11:28), illustrating a complex relationship.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 11:29 states that God's gifts and calling are revocable.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance' (Romans 11:29), meaning they are not withdrawn or regretted.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 11:32 concludes that all people have been confined to disobedience.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all' (Romans 11:32), indicating universal disobedience.

questions.question: How does Romans 11:21 function as a warning to believers?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee' (Romans 11:21), reminding believers to remain humble.

questions.question: What is the main theme of Romans 11:16 regarding the holiness of the firstfruit?
options: It is irrelevant to the branches
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches' (Romans 11:16), emphasizing the significance of holiness.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 11:10 describes the people's eyes being opened to see.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see' (Romans 11:10), indicating a state of blindness rather than sight.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:14 suggest about Paul's desire for his fellow Israelites?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses a desire to 'provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them' (Romans 11:14), indicating his longing for their salvation.

hard.title: Romans Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 11.

questions.question: What mystery concerning Israel does Paul mention in Romans 11:25?
questions.explanation: Paul states that blindness in part has happened to Israel until the fulness of the Gentiles comes in (Romans 11:25).

questions.question: According to Romans 11:26, who is the Deliverer that will turn away ungodliness from Jacob?
questions.explanation: The Deliverer referred to in Romans 11:26 is understood to be Jesus, who fulfills the promise of turning away ungodliness from Jacob.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:29 say about the gifts and calling of God?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:29 states that the gifts and calling of God are without repentance, meaning they cannot be taken back.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the relationship between Israel and the Gentiles in Romans 11:30?
options: Gentiles obtained mercy through Israel's unbelief
questions.correctAnswer: Gentiles obtained mercy through Israel's unbelief
questions.explanation: Romans 11:30 explains that Gentiles have obtained mercy through the unbelief of the Israelites.

questions.question: In Romans 11:31, what is the purpose of Israel's unbelief according to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul states that through the unbelief of Israel, the Gentiles may also obtain mercy (Romans 11:31).

questions.question: According to Romans 11:33, how does Paul describe the wisdom and knowledge of God?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses the depth of the riches of God's wisdom and knowledge as unsearchable (Romans 11:33).

questions.question: What literary device is used by Paul in Romans 11:22 when discussing God's goodness and severity?
questions.explanation: Paul uses a form of parallelism in Romans 11:22 to contrast God's goodness and severity toward different groups.

questions.question: What is the fate of those branches that do not abide in belief according to Romans 11:23?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:23 indicates that those branches that do not abide in belief will be cut off.

questions.question: In Romans 11:36, what does Paul affirm about all things?
options: All things are for the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Romans 11:36 declares that all things are of God, through God, and to God.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 11:28 states that as concerning the gospel, the Israelites are considered enemies.
questions.explanation: Romans 11:28 indicates that concerning the gospel, the Israelites are enemies for the sake of the Gentiles.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 11:24 teaches that Gentiles are naturally part of the olive tree.
questions.explanation: Romans 11:24 explains that Gentiles are wild by nature and are grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Romans 11:26 regarding Israel's salvation?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:26 references the promise of the Deliverer turning away ungodliness from Jacob, which connects with Isaiah 59:20.

questions.question: What does the term 'remnant' in Romans 11:5 signify in relation to God's people?
questions.explanation: The 'remnant' in Romans 11:5 refers to a small group of faithful individuals who have remained true to God.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:1 indicate about God's relationship with Israel?
options: God has cast away His people
God has not cast away His people
God is indifferent to Israel's fate
questions.correctAnswer: God has not cast away His people
questions.explanation: Romans 11:1 states, 'Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.' This emphasizes that God has not rejected Israel, affirming His ongoing covenantal relationship.

questions.question: According to Romans 11:6, what is the relationship between grace and works?
options: Grace is not based on works
Works and grace are the same
questions.correctAnswer: Grace is not based on works
questions.explanation: Romans 11:6 explains that if salvation is by grace, it cannot be based on works, highlighting the unmerited nature of grace in salvation.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:11 suggest about the purpose of Israel's stumbling?
options: It was to lead to their destruction
It was to bring salvation to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It was to bring salvation to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Romans 11:11 states that through Israel's fall, salvation has come to the Gentiles, indicating a divine purpose in their stumbling.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:25 teach about the blindness of Israel?
options: It is a mystery until the Gentiles come in
It is a sign of God's judgment only
It is the final state of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It is a mystery until the Gentiles come in
questions.explanation: Romans 11:25 reveals that the blindness in part has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, indicating a temporary condition.

questions.question: In Romans 11:16, what analogy is used to describe the relationship between the holy root and branches?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:16 uses the analogy of a root and branches to illustrate the connection between the holy root (God's promise) and the branches (believers).

questions.question: What does Romans 11:22 warn about God's nature?
options: God shows both goodness and severity
questions.correctAnswer: God shows both goodness and severity
questions.explanation: Romans 11:22 highlights the dual aspects of God's character, showing both His goodness to those who believe and severity to those who fall.

questions.question: According to Romans 11:30, how have Gentiles obtained mercy?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:30 states that Gentiles have obtained mercy through the unbelief of Israel, highlighting God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What aspect of God is revealed in Romans 11:33 regarding His wisdom?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:33 declares the depth of the riches of God's wisdom and knowledge, emphasizing that His judgments and ways are beyond human understanding.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:28 say about the relationship between Israel and the Gospel?
options: They are indifferent to the Gospel
They are enemies for the sake of the Gentiles
They have fully accepted the Gospel
questions.correctAnswer: They are enemies for the sake of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Romans 11:28 indicates that as concerning the Gospel, Israel are enemies for the Gentiles' sake, which shows the tension in God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:14 express as a motivation for Paul's ministry?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:14 reveals that Paul seeks to provoke Israel to jealousy, aiming to save some of them by demonstrating the grace given to the Gentiles.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:24 imply about the natural branches of the olive tree?
options: They can be grafted back in
questions.correctAnswer: They can be grafted back in
questions.explanation: Romans 11:24 suggests that if the wild branches can be grafted into the olive tree, the natural branches (Israel) can also be grafted back in, emphasizing God's mercy.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:15 suggest about the casting away of Israel?
options: It brings reconciliation to the world
questions.correctAnswer: It brings reconciliation to the world
questions.explanation: Romans 11:15 states that the casting away of Israel leads to the reconciling of the world, underscoring the redemptive purpose in God's plan.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Romans 11:7 and Romans 11:8 convey about Israel's condition?
options: Israel has no connection to God
questions.explanation: Romans 11:7 and 11:8 together illustrate that Israel has not obtained what it seeks and has been given a spirit of slumber, resulting in spiritual blindness.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:29 state about God's gifts and calling?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:29 teaches that God's gifts and calling are irrevocable, affirming His faithfulness to His promises and the covenant.

questions.question: What does Romans 11:36 reveal about the ultimate purpose of all things?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:36 concludes that all things are from, through, and to God, emphasizing that the ultimate purpose of creation is to glorify Him.
